newsitem.title: JAPAN: SHOWA YOKKAICHI FIRE-HIT TOPPER TO RESTART AUG 17.
newsitem.headline: SHOWA YOKKAICHI FIRE-HIT TOPPER TO RESTART AUG 17.

text.p: Showa Yokkaichi Sekiyu Co Ltd said on Wednesday its 150,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) crude distillation unit in central Japan, which has been closed since a fire on Monday, is expected to resume operations as early as August 17.

"We are likely to be able to restart the topper around this Sunday as we have recieved permission to do so and it will take just a few more days for us to take care of the damage from the fire," a company official said.
A minor fire broke out at the plant in Yokkaichi, Mie Prefecture, on Monday afternoon, when heated residue oil leaked from a pipe extending from the unit and caught fire.
The local fire department, which had ordered Showa Yokkaichi to suspend operation of the topper after the fire, gave the green light on Wednesday morning for the topper to restart.
The fire did not affect operations at the plant's other topper, with a crude processing capacity of 90,000 bpd.
The incident has not disrupted production plans at the Showa Shell Sekiyu KK group, to which Showa Yokkaichi belongs, a Showa Shell spokesman said.
Showa Shell Sekiyu, an oil refiner and distributor, is owned 50 percent by the Royal Dutch/Shell Group.
